grafias_do_espelho: $64.4 MILLION · LUMP SUMS AS EACH DAM CAME INTO SERVICE · 60 YEARS OF FLOOD CONTROL
50% OF THE EXPECTED U.S. FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTED
Source: USACE & BPA, 2013; Columbia River Treaty, Art. IV and VI
texto_aprovado: Then follow the money, because it runs the other way. Water comes down, and money goes up. For the room behind the Canadian dams, the United States paid 64.4 million dollars in lump sums, as each dam came into service, for 60 years of flood protection. The price was half of what those dams were expected to save it in flood damage. Most of the money was for one lake: Arrow, the lake at the start of this story.
